voiceover: Entry two. Replies are arriving in four different places. Norah's Notebook, entry two. The story is fiction. The fix is real. Last time: Mara merged four tabs, and overnight the count changed. Dear notebook: nine weeks to go. The count moved because replies arrived. The family group chat. A voicemail. A direct message. A card in the mail. Nobody did anything wrong. They replied the easy way. Then Eli's cousin said yes in the chat, and no by voicemail. Two answers, two places. Which one counted? Here's the part people skip. Guests reply wherever the invitation found them. Rule one: print exactly where replies go. One address, one number. Emily Post says an email reply is fine, as long as it's an option. Rule two: one RSVP deadline. Count back from the caterer. Caterers usually need final headcounts one to two weeks before the wedding. Leave at least ten days between your RSVP deadline and that date. Mara's caterer says two weeks. Her deadline lands just over three weeks out. Then confirm the date with your caterer. If it's your winter wedding too, follow along. Tomorrow, I'll show you what a guest sees. This is the step people skip. Rule three: one channel for everyone. Text one invitation, text them all. That's etiquette specialist Anne Chertoff's advice. For a reply in the wrong place, I'd say this. Thank you! So we don't lose your reply, could you send it the way the invitation says? Tonight Mara moved every stray reply into one list. One path. One date. One channel. I'm Norah, an AI character, and this is Wedillybird. The pen crosses out the group chat, and writes the next problem. A maybe arrives with a heart emoji.

caption:
How to track wedding RSVPs: one reply path and an RSVP deadline counted back from the caterer.
Entry 02 of Norah's Notebook: replies in four places, three rules, and a word-for-word message for stray replies.
Fiction: Norah and the couple are invented. The tips are real.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment: Three rules: 1) Print exactly where replies go: one address or one number (Emily Post says an email reply is fine as an option). 2) One RSVP deadline: count back from your caterer's final headcount date and leave at least ten days (Joy, 2025), then confirm the date with your caterer. 3) One channel for everyone: if you text one invitation, text them all (Anne Chertoff, Business Insider, 2021). Message for a stray reply, copy and paste: "Thank you! So we don't lose your reply, could you send it the way the invitation says?" Fiction: Mara, Eli and Norah are invented; the tips are real. Norah is AI-generated.
comment_bait: Where do most of your replies land: chat, text, email or mail?

sources.fact: Venues and caterers typically need final headcounts one to two weeks before the wedding; set the RSVP deadline at least ten days before that headcount date so you have time to chase

sources.fact: Confirm the headcount date with your caterer (the same Joy article is internally inconsistent, 3-4 weeks vs 2-3 weeks before the wedding)

sources.fact: It is acceptable to give guests the option of replying by email, as long as it is an option (print the address on the response card)
sources.title: Wedding Email Dos and Don'ts

sources.fact: Etiquette specialist Anne Chertoff would never recommend texting someone a wedding invitation unless everyone is getting a text (exception: a spontaneous celebration after a city-hall wedding)
